status_summary: In April 2026 VA spokespeople said average waits for existing patients were lower than in fiscal 2024 and that VA had allowed more flexible off-hours appointment scheduling, and the administration has sought to expand community care. An analysis of new-patient waits at 134 medical centers, reported in the same article from VA data supplied to an advocacy group, showed mixed results, and the article did not mention provider productivity targets. No order setting a patients-per-provider requirement was found.

timeline.event: VA spokespeople said wait times had stabilized or fallen and that more flexible off-hours scheduling had been allowed, while reported VA data showed mixed new-patient wait results.

title: Bring VHA wait times into MISSION Act time frames through workflow changes
uncertainties: The wait-time statements are VA spokesperson claims relayed by a news outlet, and the underlying data in that article came from VA records supplied to an advocacy group; neither was independently verified, and the date of the statements is taken from the article. Extended-hours clinics predate this term (a VA News release of 2024-05-24 describes Access Sprints with night and weekend clinics), so they are not counted as new action. Searches covered VA productivity directives and found no patients-per-provider requirement; a directive could exist that was not public.
